title: Trump Just Put His Housing Regulator in Charge of 18 Spy Agencies. The CIA Was Already at War With Itself.
excerpt: Bill Pulte, who has no intelligence experience, replaces the departing Tulsi Gabbard as acting DNI while the US is fighting Iran, the CIA has stopped cooperating with its oversight body, and oil prices are at a one-week high.
body:
President Donald Trump on Tuesday appointed Bill Pulte, the 38-year-old director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, as acting director of national intelligence — putting a political loyalist with no known intelligence experience in charge of America's 18-agency spy apparatus at a time when the country is fighting a war in Iran and its own intelligence agencies have stopped cooperating with each other.

In a post on his Truth Social platform, Trump said Pulte "has deep experience managing the most sensitive matters in America, the safety and soundness of the Markets, and over 10 Trillion Dollars at Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac." Pulte will continue serving as FHFA director and chairman of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac while holding the acting intelligence post — an unusual doubling of responsibilities during a period of active military engagement.

## Why Gabbard Left

Tulsi Gabbard, the outgoing director of national intelligence, announced her resignation on May 22, citing her husband Abraham Williams' diagnosis of "an extremely rare form of bone cancer." She will remain in her position until June 30.

Reuters reported that Gabbard was effectively pushed from the role over friction with the White House. Her isolationist tendencies — which had originally attracted Trump during her shift from the Democratic Party to the MAGA movement — put her at odds with his military actions in Iran and Venezuela. She was routinely sidelined from major foreign policy decisions in Trump's second term, and much of her focus in office revolved around what she described as rooting out "deep state" actors within the intelligence community.

## The CIA Has Stopped Cooperating

The appointment arrives at a particularly volatile moment for America's intelligence infrastructure. According to a Reuters investigation published on Tuesday, the CIA has stopped contributing to some intelligence assessments produced by the Office of the Director of National Intelligence — including assessments related to the Iran war.

The breakdown stems from a year-long turf war between the CIA, led by Director John Ratcliffe, and Gabbard's office. At the centre of the dispute is a task force Gabbard created in April 2025 called the Director's Initiatives Group, which the CIA contends acted recklessly by circumventing traditional intelligence-sharing protocols.

The two agencies now operate as "largely separate analytical operations," Reuters reported, citing four people with direct knowledge of the matter. The CIA at one point stopped publishing National Intelligence Council reports on the internal distribution service it controls.

Beth Sanner, a former deputy director of national intelligence during Trump's first term, warned that the dysfunction could lead to intelligence failures. "When you're not doing that, then you set up the potential that agencies are just going to kind of pull back into their stove pipes," she said.

## The India Angle

For India, the American intelligence shake-up matters for two immediate reasons. First, the Iran war has effectively shut the Strait of Hormuz, through which more than 40 per cent of India's crude oil imports previously flowed. Any disruption to the quality of American intelligence assessments on Iran — now confirmed by Reuters — raises the risk of miscalculation in a conflict that directly affects India's energy security and economic stability.

Goldman Sachs last week named India the most vulnerable major economy to the Hormuz disruption, estimating a potential GDP hit of 3.6 per cent. Foreign investors have pulled more money out of India in the first five months of 2026 than they did in all of 2025.

Second, Gabbard herself was one of the most prominent Indian-origin figures in American political life. A Hindu practitioner who invoked the Bhagavad Gita when she was sworn in as a congresswoman in 2013, her departure removes a figure who — for all the controversies of her tenure — represented a kind of cultural visibility for the Indian diaspora at the highest levels of the US national security establishment.

## What Pulte Brings

Pulte is best known for managing Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac and for spearheading a Trump proposal to create 50-year mortgage terms — a plan that was abandoned after widespread criticism. He has no known background in intelligence collection, analysis, or national security.

Critics were swift. Ned Price, a former CIA analyst and State Department official, noted that Pulte "earned Trump's trust by using mortgage records to pursue perceived political enemies. Now this top henchman will have access to some of our most sensitive intelligence and exquisite capabilities."

The Government Accountability Office announced in December that it was investigating whether Pulte abused his FHFA position and government resources to target Trump adversaries.

As acting director, Pulte does not require Senate confirmation. Trump has not said whether he will nominate a permanent replacement.

*Sources: Reuters, CNN, USA Today, The Daily Caller, Military.com*
author: Diaspora Desk
